mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained increases in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous month signals increased consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight monetary policy coupled with a strong labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and wage pressures.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the previous month indicates a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the previous six months signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 0.5%.
